classification.difficultyReason: Identify inferred dimensions and calculate the same composite area using both addition and subtraction.

content.prompt: Find the area of the following figure, using two different methods.

spec.description: Unshaded hexagon consisting of lower-left and upper-right square regions and two intervening right triangles. Retains both red dashed construction segments, all four 4 cm labels and all three right-angle marks. Decorative blue boundary ink is replaced with house black.
spec.mathematics: Boundary vertices in a centimetre coordinate model are (0,0), (4,0), (8,4), (8,8), (4,8), (0,4). Construction segments x=4 and y=4 meet perpendicularly. The two square regions have side 4 cm and both triangular regions have perpendicular legs 4 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and supplied construction lines are visible; no calculated areas or extra dimensions appear.

answer.short:
$48\text{ cm}^2$.

Add two squares and two right triangles, or subtract two right triangles from an enclosing square.
answer.worked:
Method 1: add the areas. The dashed lines divide the figure into two squares of side $4$ cm and two right triangles, each with base and perpendicular height $4$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=2(4\times4)+2\left(\frac12\times4\times4\right)\\\text{Area}&=32+16\\\text{Area}&=48\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
Method 2: subtract the areas. Complete an enclosing square of side $4+4=8$ cm. The two missing corner triangles each have base and perpendicular height $4$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=8\times8-2\left(\frac12\times4\times4\right)\\\text{Area}&=64-16\\\text{Area}&=48\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
